data.title: TOP Financial moves global headquarters to Houston, eyes U.S. growth
data.description:
• TOP Financial (TOP) announced on Friday that it will relocate its global headquarters to Houston, Texas, as it shifts its corporate focus toward the U.S. market.
  • The company said the move will bring it closer to its AI business, strategic partners, and U.S. talent while supporting expansion in North America.
  • It will complete the relocation in phases over the coming months, with its other regional offices continuing to operate.
  • The company said the transition will not disrupt services for existing clients or partners.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Beyond Meat recovers after seven straight sessions of losses
data.description:
Beyond Meat (BYND) recovered some ground on Friday as its shares raced 4.61% to settle at $11.79 after declining for seven consecutive sessions.

The plant-based meat maker suffered heavy losses this week, with shares ending 6.39% lower on Tuesday while registering a 7.07% loss the following day.

Between August 27 and September 3, the stock erased nearly 20% of its value. On a YTD basis, it has plunged nearly 55% compared to a 13% rise in broader markets.

As per Seeking Alpha’s quant ratings, the company is currently categorized as Strong Sell with a score of 1.05 out of 5. BYND has been graded a C+ for valuation and a B- for profitability. Seeking Alpha and Wall Street analysts have issued a Sell call for the company.

The selloff comes as the California-based firm continues to be mired in revenue declines, weak gross margins, and minimal pricing power in its core U.S. market.

In early August,  Beyond Meat executed a 1-for-30 reverse stock split to regain compliance with Nasdaq’s minimum bid price requirement and maintain its listing.

Analysts hold a bearish view of the stock with weak prospects and see minimal chances of the company achieving a successful turnaround. They foresee continued downside in the stock price going forward.

“Beyond Meat stock has been a perennial underperformer since its IPO in 2019. Whilst there aren't any near-term critical liquidity risks, I find it highly unlikely the business will be able to reverse the current course of widening losses and declining revenue,” Seeking Alpha analyst  Eborose Capital said in a recent note.

What Happened to lululemon

Lululemon reported Q2 fiscal 2026 results on September 3, posting GAAP EPS of $2.92 on revenue of $2.42 billion. While EPS beat expectations by $1.13, revenue missed by $40 million. Management simultaneously slashed its full-year revenue and EPS outlook, citing softening demand trends across both North America and China Mainland.

Management attributed Q2 demand weakness to negative media and social-media commentary, softer-than-planned new-product launches, and weaker store traffic.

data.title: AstraZeneca wins approval of camizestrant for breast cancer
data.description:
• The US FDA has granted accelerated approval to AstraZeneca's (AZN) Etcamah (camizestrant) in combination with a CDK4/6 inhibitor (abemaciclib, palbociclib, or ribociclib) for HR+, HER2- breast cancer.
  • The approval is for those with a estrogen receptor-1 (ESR1) mutation which can be discovered during aromatase inhibitor and CDK 4/6 inhibitor therapy based on a test.
  • Approval was based on a trial that showed the camizestrant combo improved median progression-free survival vs. an aromatase inhibitor in combination with a CDK4/6 inhibitor. Estimated median progression-free survival was 16 months in the camizestrant combo arm compared to 9.2 months in the aromatase inhibitor combo arm.
  • The FDA also approved the Guardant Health (GH) Guardant360 CDx assay as a companion diagnostic device to determine breast cancer patients with the ESR1 mutation who would benefit from camizestrant.

data.title: Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs close to bagging top roles in Anthropic IPO - report
data.description:
Anthropic (ANTHRO) is said to be nearing a deal with Morgan Stanley (MS) and Goldman Sachs (GS) for top roles in the AI giant's blockbuster IPO.

Morgan Stanley could bag the "lead left"—the strategic adviser on the deal—role, four people familiar with the matter told the Financial Times. 

MS had held talks with potential Anthropic investors over the IPO price recently, according to two of the sources.

Goldman Sachs could be the IPO's stabilization agent. JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Citigroup (C), and Barclays (BCS) are also expected to get leading roles in the IPO, the report published on Friday noted.

The Claude chatbot owner is expected to file its IPO publicly, which could value the company over $2 trillion, as soon as next week, several sources reportedly said.

A roadshow could come near September-end, people familiar with the matter told the FT. Anthropic could begin trading in New York in late September or early October.

data.title: Sandisk leads Nasdaq's weekly gainers; Autodesk drags

data.title: The Trade Desk ends 4.5% lower, snapping a six-session winning streak
data.description:
The Trade Desk (TTD) ended 4.5% lower at $14.41 on Friday, snapping a six-session winning streak during which the stock gained 15.8%.

The stock last closed lower on Aug. 26, when it ended at $13.03.

Shares fell on Friday after the digital advertising platform said in a filing that it plans to cut roughly 15% of its workforce as part of an organizational restructuring. The headcount reductions are expected to be substantially completed in the third quarter of 2026.

The company expects to incur about $39 million to $51 million in cash restructuring and related charges, mainly for employee severance and benefits, partially offset by a $4 million to $5 million reversal related to stock-based compensation.

The stock remains down 61% year to date.

Following a second-quarter revenue miss, CEO Jeff Green said the results “did not meet the standard we set for ourselves,” citing a complex environment for marketers. The company has said it is working to improve execution and invest in artificial intelligence and measurement. In early August, the company reported second-quarter adjusted earnings of $0.34 per share, below analysts' expectations of $0.40.

data.title: 3 things to look out for on Tuesday
data.description:
Wall Street's major market averages finished lower on Friday after traders and investors digested the latest jobs data, which came in stronger than forecasted.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) ended -0.5%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) handed back -0.3%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) lost -0.2%.

The U.S. stock market will be closed Monday for observance of the Labor Day holiday.

Now, here are three things to look out for on Tuesday:

  • Nike (NKE) will hold its annual meeting. The key shareholder votes of interest will be on a proposal for a stock purchase plan expansion and a proposal on meeting environmental targets.
  • Shareholders with AtaiBeckley (ATAI) will vote on the buyout offer from Eli Lilly (LLY).
  • GameStop (GME) is slated to post second-quarter results after the closing bell. The company this past week delivered preliminary numbers.
